issues: What elements establish a prima facie case of discrimination on the basis of disability in employment
Whether refusing a modified work schedule without inquiry into the disability constitutes discrimination
What is the scope and standard of the duty to accommodate a disabled employee to the point of undue hardship
What procedural obligations (individualized assessment, exploring options) does an employer have when responding to an accommodation request
What factors are relevant to determining undue hardship in a federally regulated workplace
What remedies are available for failure to accommodate under federal human rights legislation
key_facts: Employee works for a federally regulated bank
Employee requested a modified work schedule as accommodation
Employer did not investigate or inquire into the request before refusing
causes_of_action: Discrimination in employment on the basis of disability
Failure to accommodate to the point of undue hardship
search_terms: Moore v British Columbia test discrimination
undue hardship factors Canadian Human Rights Act
